title: Brevo vs. ActiveCampaign 2026: Pricing & Features Compared
snippet:
I asked Brevo’s AI automation builder to do the same as ActiveCampaign: “create an automation for abandoned cart visitors who added $500 or more to their carts,” but it failed to produce what I asked and gave me a blank canvas instead, so I switched to the pre-built template.

FAQs Key takeaways Brevo is good value for large lists, and ActiveCampaign offers value when your send-per-contact ratio is high Neither tool has unlimited emails or access to all features; there are send limits and add-ons in both ActiveCampaign offers its more advanced AI and ecommerce features at a lower price point than Brevo Transactional email and SMS are more accessible in Brevo, supported in all plans rather than through add-ons The automation win is ActiveCampaign's due to its 950+ automation recipes and a more capable AI that builds working flows for you Show more Ecommerce marketers should look to Brevo for storing a large list and sending infrequently due to paying for email volume. ActiveCampaign’s contact-based pricing is higher at the same list size, but with more sends included. What does that mean? That you pick based on how often you email when cost is the important factor. Brevo (Sendinblue up to May 2023) stores 500,000 contacts for $32/month with 20,000 sends. ActiveCampaign supports 10–15 emails per contact. The two also diverge in ecommerce fit, and they have plan feature restrictions and add-ons that change the value proposition. Below: a Brevo vs. ActiveCampaign comparison of costs per 1,000, 2,500, 10,000, and 20,000 contacts, plans, features, and use cases. Brevo or ActiveCampaign: the short answer ActiveCampaign is suited to ecommerce and a list that you message frequently, such as 10 times each month. Brevo is a cheaper pick for storing thousands of contacts and sending to them infrequently, such as two or three times each month. Brevo and ActiveCampaign pricing comparison Brevo has a lower cost at all contact tiers in comparable plans because it charges by monthly email volume. The contact-based pricing of ActiveCampaign climbs with your list size, but could suit you better if you send lots of emails per contact.
